subject: Media Literacy
title: Online Echo Chambers and Extremism
description: A 60-second lesson on Online Echo Chambers and Extremism.

hook.text: A lonely teenager joins an online group for like-minded people. Six months later, his views are unrecognizable.

buildup.text: Online communities can provide belonging. But closed communities can also drive ideological escalation.

discovery.text: Group polarization means that like-minded groups shift toward more extreme versions of their shared views.

twist.text: Platforms recommend these communities to new users, algorithmically funneling curious people toward radical groups.

climax.text: The path from curiosity to extremism is shorter online than most people realize.

punchline.text: The community gave him belonging. It also gave him extremism.

quiz.question: What is group polarization?
options: Groups naturally become more moderate over time
Like-minded groups shift toward more extreme versions of their shared views
Groups always split into opposing factions
